tagline: Along the Mettawee through the slate towns to a battlefield.
intro: At the roundabout in Manchester Center, Route 30 turns northwest and follows the Mettawee River through the Taconic Mountains, by Dorset, Pawlet and Wells. Pawlet takes its name from the river, which the earliest maps called the Paulet.

This is stone country. Dorset holds America's oldest marble quarry, and the Taconics are Vermont's slate-producing region. At Poultney the road turns north, crosses US 4 at Castleton, and runs along the east shore of Lake Bomoseen in Hubbardton, where the only battle fought in Vermont during the Revolution took place in July 1777.

moments.title: Dorset
moments.text: Marble from the quarries here went into the New York Public Library's main building. The East Dorset quarry has closed and serves in summer as a swimming hole.

moments.title: Poultney
moments.text: Once a hub of the slate trade, the town still shows it in slate sidewalks and slate fences along its streets.

moments.title: Hubbardton Battlefield
moments.text: On Monument Hill the American rear guard held off the British, until German grenadiers came up singing hymns to a military band to seem more numerous than they were.

sources.label: Vermont Tourism, 72 Hours in Rutland and Vermont's Stone Valley
